caption: A Los Angeles Rams cheerleader raises pom-poms overhead, smiling, on the field.
Zuwayda, Gaza Intense flames and smoke rise after an Israeli airstrike that destroyed several homes and tents where displaced Palestinians were staying.

Strathdon, Scotland Highland dancers compete during the Lonach Highland Gathering and Games. The annual traditional Scottish festival is held on the fourth Saturday of August in Bellabeg Park, organised by the Lonach Highland and Friendly Society (founded in 1823). It is famed for the iconic March of the Lonach Highlanders.
Singapore An aircraft departing Changi airport is silhouetted against the sun at sunrise.
Pflug, Germany A man tries to pull his opponent over the table during the traditional German finger-pulling (Fingerhakeln) championships.
Nairobi, Kenya Fans of manga, anime and Japanese culture cheer as they watch performances from cosplayers during the Otamatsuri convention.
Beijing, China A Galbot humanoid robot takes part in a tennis exhibition match against a human player during the opening ceremony for the second World Humanoid Robot Games.
Singapore Paddlers race in outrigger canoes during the IVF World Sprint Championships 2026 at Marina Bayfront.
Sade village, Indonesia A drone view shows the aftermath at a traditional Sasak village that caught fire overnight in Lombok, West Nusa Tenggara province.

La Guaira, Venezuela Veterinarians check a dog rescued from destroyed buildings after recent 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes, in the Misión Nevado temporary shelter. Venezuela was struck by two earthquakes on 24 June, which left at least 6,438 people dead. Nearly two months later, pets rescued from the rubble remain in temporary shelters, waiting to be reunited with their former owners or their new adoptive families.
Glendale, US The Arizona Cardinals cheerleaders perform before the pre-season NFL game against the Dallas Cowboys at State Farm Stadium in Arizona.

Guangyuan, China Tourists visit the Thousand Buddha cliffside statues scenic area in Sichuan province. On the east bank of the Jialing River north of Guangyuan city, the site is the largest grotto complex in Sichuan province, with carvings dating from the Northern Wei dynasty to the Qing dynasty spanning over 1,500 years.
Gaza The Israeli army demolishes buildings east of Deir al-Balah in the central Gaza Strip.

St Mullins, Ireland A satirical sculpture of Donald Trump entitled The Trash Talker by the Wexford artist TinKicker, made in protest against the US president’s forthcoming visit to Ireland, as part of the Can-al Fest street art festival in Co Carlow.
Johannesburg, South Africa A man dances before a rugby union match between South Africa and New Zealand at Ellis Park stadium.
Kolpino, Russia A person walking as smoke rises over a logistics centre after being hit by Ukrainian drones – in front of a billboard promoting contract army service.
Istanbul, Turkey Swimmers competing in the 38th Bosphorus cross-continental swimming race, which starts at Kanlıca Pier on the Asian side and finishes in Kuruçeşme on the European side.
Beijing, China Technicians carry a robot out of the ring after the free combat event of the World Humanoid Robot Games.

Amsterdam, Netherlands Audience members wave the flags of the city of Amsterdam as musicians perform the song The City of Amsterdam. The 44th edition of the Prinsengrachtconcert takes place on a floating stage on the Prinsengracht in front of Hotel Pulitzer, the largest free open-air classical music concert in the Netherlands.
Rimas, a teen who lost both legs, floats on her back during swimming training in a pool.

Kyiv, Ukraine Smoke rising in the city during a Russian drone strike. A heavy Russian missile and drone bombardment killed at least 16 people in and around the city in one of the most intense aerial attacks on Ukraine’s capital since the start of the war.

Kyiv, Ukraine Charred books after a fire at the country’s biggest book market, caused by a Russian missile attack. The Ukrainian Book Institute has called on the international publishing community to support Ukrainian publishers after Russian attacks in July and early August destroyed about 10m books and a significant share of the country’s book production capacity.

Kyiv, Ukraine People take shelter and sleep inside a subway station during an air raid alert. Russia and Ukraine have been escalating long-range attacks recently while air defences remain short. Ukraine has attacked oil refineries and warehouses close to Moscow using newly developed cruise missiles and drones, while Russia has stepped up its attacks on Kyiv, making heavy use of hard ballistics.

Moscow, Russia Drivers line up at a Lukoil petrol station in the capital, where many other stations have run out of fuel . Moscow confirmed this week that Russia was having to import refined petroleum products to try to stabilise supply following Ukraine’s attacks on its refineries. The Reuters news agency used industry contacts and market data to establish that a tanker from India had recently arrived and unloaded, while supplies were also being sourced from east Asia.

Podolsk, Russia A helicopter prepares to drop water during a fire at Wildberries’ logistics complex. Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks since the start of the war, causing a fire at a distribution warehouse near Moscow and killing at least six people overnight, according to Russian authorities.

Gaza Palestinians remove iron from the rubble of buildings destroyed by Israeli airstrikes to repair and recycle it. Benjamin Netanyahu told Donald Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner there can be no progress on the stalled Gaza ceasefire deal or an Israeli withdrawal from the coastal strip until Hamas first disarms.

Khan Younis, Gaza Rimas Abu Shalouf, 16, who lost both legs after being injured during the Israel offensive, receives swimming training from the Heal Palestine organisation. Israel has killed more than 1,200 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded more than 4,100 since agreeing to the ceasefire on 10 October 2025, according to Gaza’s health ministry.

Oakland, California, US Protesters and campaigners gather for the federal trial against Meta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, at the district court. Meta has taken a ‘don’t ask, don’t tell’ strategy when it comes to the safety of children on its social media platforms, according to a whistleblower who testified during the landmark trial this week.

London, England Attendees hold flowers and placards during a vigil for former Cambridge professor Jason Arday in Trafalgar Square, after he was found dead at his home in south London. Arday’s family said in a statement: ‘Jason was subjected to a campaign of sustained abuse for more than three years since he accepted the role of professor at Cambridge University by those who would leave no stone unturned in their quest to undermine him. The campaign of misinformation was too much for Jason, who was a gentle man and always wanted to see the best in everyone’.

London, England A homeless man on a street in central London. Prime minister Andy Burnham has urged local leaders to offer all rough sleepers in England a route off the streets by Christmas, as he pledges another £100m to end street homelessness.
Quibdó, Colombia Buildings destroyed during last week’s earthquake in the Medrano neighbourhood of the city.

Ruteng, Indonesia Children observe the damage at St Fransiskus Asisi-Karot church, in the aftermath of an earthquake. Rescue crews dug through collapsed buildings and landslide debris in eastern Indonesia as they searched for bodies and possible survivors after a powerful earthquake killed at least 53 people, injured more than 100 and displaced thousands.

Salamina, Greece A firefighter walks towards a house engulfed with flames during a wildfire on the island. Wildfires are projected to burn 39% more of Europe by the end of the century even in the best-case scenario for stopping the planet from heating, a study has found , unless action is taken to manage them better.
Waimes, Belgium Belgian firefighters work in a forest affected by a wildfire.

Kandahar, Afghanistan A woman uses a smartphone to film celebrations marking the fifth anniversary of the Taliban governments’s return to power. The United Nations described a recent ‘cascade of [Taliban] edicts and laws’ that have banned women from universities and most employment, denied teenage girls education and imposed strict dress codes.

Kabul, Afghanistan A boy holds an AK-style rifle during celebrations marking the fifth anniversary of the US withdrawal from Afghanistan. Five years after the Taliban took power , an increasing number of countries are renewing ties or scaling up diplomatic contacts with the hardline Islamists, who seized power in Kabul in 2021 after 20 years of brutal insurgent warfare.
Iga-Barrière, Democratic Republic of the Congo People search for gold at a mining site.

Lake Tuz, Turkey Visitors wade in the vibrant pink shallows. The water’s striking colour during the summer is believed to be caused by an increase in salinity, high temperatures and microalgae that produce betacarotene as a protective shield.

Yaounde, Cameroon A Cameroon player kisses a boy on his forehead during a parade after the Indomitable Lionesses became only the fourth country to lift the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations. Cameroon had not reached a Wafcon final in a decade and had never even scored a goal in the final, but had three before half-time against Malawi.
Budapest, Hungary A member of Team Russia performs a somersault during the final of the World Aquatics Junior Artistic Swimming Championships.
Giant panda cub twins Leni and Lotti arrive for a media at the Zoo in Berlin, Germany.

Ceuta, Spain Police officers stand guard near a group of migrants on El Trampolín beach. Authorities in Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta cleared people from the site on Friday while crews cleaned the area. The Spanish government is providing temporary shelter for 1,800 people sleeping rough on the beach.

Stellenbosch, South Africa Indian Runner Ducks are herded to forage for aphids, worms and snails at the Vergenoegd wine farm. Every morning, 1,000 long-necked ducks are let loose on a South African wine farm to gobble up insects in an environmentally friendly method of pest control that is gaining popularity.

Grebenac, Serbia A man rides a scooter beneath a smoke-filled sky as a wildfire burns in the Deliblatska Peščara nature reserve, about 70km (43 miles) north-east of Belgrade. Firefighters are battling wildfires across the Balkans as days of high temperatures and drought conditions continue to drive blazes in several countries.
Zandvoort, the Netherlands Spectators sit in the stands before a practice session for the Formula One Dutch Grand Prix.

Shuyang, China Visitors walk around the interior of a tulou roundhouse – a large, fortified earthen dwelling built by the Hakka people between the 12th and 20th centuries – in Fujian province. In recent years, Nanjing county has sought to revitalise its Hakka heritage by integrating culture and tourism.
Les Deux Alpes, France A view of Lake Chambon in the rain, from the Chambon dam.

Chester, UK A 15ft-long python named after the actor Jodie Foster is believed to be the first snake in the world to benefit from a cancer treatment normally used on humans. Vets at Chester zoo said the reptile was back to her ‘bright and feisty self’ after undergoing electrochemotherapy for a cancerous tumour on her jawbone.
Auckland, New Zealand A model walks the runway for the Tāwhiao label during the Kāhui Collective show at New Zealand fashion week.
Budry, Poland Members of Polish and German armed forces install concrete anti-tank obstacles as part of the East Shield fortifications along the Polish border with the Russian exclave Kaliningrad.
Guwahati, India A cycle rickshaw driver navigates through flood waters after heavy monsoon rains.
Chattogram, Bangladesh Stacks of hilsa fish stand at Rani Rashmoni Ghat. The salted and cured fish is a culinary tradition in Bengali cuisine.
Berlin, Germany Giant panda twins Leni, right, and Lotti arrive at a media event at the city’s zoo on the eve of their second birthday.
Chernihiv region, Ukraine People greet Ukrainian soldiers returning from captivity after a prisoner exchange between Russia and Ukraine.

Khan Younis, Gaza Ahmed Abdulaziz Abu Anzeh, a 61-year-old Palestinian who has lung cancer and malnutrition, sits in a makeshift tent where he lives in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis. Israel’s closure of border crossings and restrictions on the entry of medicines into the region have made it difficult for Abu Anzeh and others like him to access the treatment they need.
Santiago region, Chile Snowboarders ride down a slope at the El Colorado ski resort in the Andes.
Seoul, South Korea Samsung employees take part in a protest to demand improvements to the company’s compensation system.
